images.caption:
Moelfamalambanana The Moel Famau Lambanana was unveiled during the Big Walk event, arranged to celebrate the connection between Liverpool and the Clwydian Range as the city celebrates being European Capital of Culture. The Clwydian Range has a strong cultural connection to Liverpool.
Back in 1926, the Crosville bus company started a service from Liverpool to Loggerheads which brought thousands of day trippers to the area.

The lambanana has been decorated by children from local schools.

images.filename: Offa's Dyke LDP nearly at Moel Famau - geograph.org.uk - 1030716.jpg
images.caption: Offa's Dyke LDP nearly at Moel Famau The last steep bit of the path leading up to the south west corner of the Jubilee Tower on Moel Famau.  The signpost indicates the direction of the Offa's Dyke LDP, which continues along the ridge.  In the snow the summit is much quieter than usual, although the small black blob between the ruin and the signpost is a collie who was enjoying his wintry walk with his master.
